questions.text: What does catastrophic forgetting mean when adapting a text LLM into a VLM?

options.A: The model consumes more context positions when image tokens are added.
options.B: The model loses previously learned text skills during multimodal adaptation.
options.C: The vision encoder produces different patch counts for different resolutions.
options.D: The training corpus includes both image-caption and interleaved documents.

questions.explanation: Catastrophic forgetting is degradation of previously learned capabilities while learning new ones, such as text-only reasoning regressing during multimodal adaptation.

questions.text: A resolution router lowers average visual-token usage. What else must you measure before claiming it preserves answer quality?

options.A: Only whether each request returns a syntactically valid answer.
options.B: Only whether the average input resolution is lower than before.
options.C: Only whether the routing tier fractions sum to one.
options.D: Task accuracy, including detail-sensitive cases routed to low resolution.

questions.explanation: Token savings alone do not establish quality preservation. Misrouting OCR or fine-detail queries can remove evidence the model needs, so task accuracy and routing failures must be evaluated.

questions.text: CorpusMix.steps computes int(total * fraction) independently for each modality. With normalized fractions 0.4, 0.35, 0.2, 0.05 and total=3, what counts result?
questions.explanation: Independent integer truncation gives int(1.2)=1, int(1.05)=1, int(0.6)=0, int(0.15)=0. No remainder allocation is implemented.
